company_news.headline: Stripe, Advent offer over $53 billion for PayPal, sources say
company_news.summary: STORY: :: Stripe and PE firm Advent have made a joint offer to acquire PayPal:: Milana Vinn, Tech M&A Correspondent:: The deal that would value PayPal at more than $53 billion:: New York/July 15, 2026"Stripe and Advent had partnered together, and our sources are telling us that they had made a bid about ten days ago, actually. And the bid would value PayPal at more than $53 billion. Exact price is $60.5 a share. This is not the first time they actually placing this bid. We have heard from sources that originally their offer, the first offer was made in early April, and the buyers have been starting PayPal since February. The reason why they are doing this is because the combination actually makes sense. Stripe is really well placed with merchant providers, and PayPal is obviously a really known consumer facing company. They have Venmo, which is peer to peer payment service, as well as they have the PayPal checkout button, which shoppers use online. So by combining the two, you essentially bringing together merchants and consumers in the same platform. So you creating your own network where payments can flow together between the consumers and the merchants. And that really is complementary for both companies. PayPal used to be a really dominant player in online payments. It still is. But during Covid and pandemic, PayPal's valuation was over 300 billion. So it's quite a departure from the prior values. The company has really struggled with the rising competition with, Apple payments and Google payments, as well as other up and coming providers. PayPal really struggled to compete and grow, and I think investors have really been concerned about the growth trajectory of the company."The offer, submitted earlier this month, is backed by about $50 billion in committed financing from banks, said one of them. The offer represents around a 28% premium to PayPal's closing share price on Tuesday.The sources declined to be named as the deal discussions are confidential. PayPal, Stripe and Advent declined to comment. Reuters first reported the news late on Tuesday.Combining Stripe and PayPal, the most widely used payment platforms for internet merchants, would create one of the world's largest global online payments company, processing some $3.7 trillion of annual payment volume.The proposal follows an initial approach made in early April, the sources said. Stripe and Advent have not received a response from PayPal and are seeking to advance discussions in the coming weeks, the sources said.
